title: Sell Mineral Rights in Pryor, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Pryor, MT
metaDescription: Pryor, MT sits at the foot of the Pryor Mountains on Crow Reservation land, mostly quiet on the mineral side. I buy trust and fee interests here honestly.
heroLead: Pryor sits up against the Pryor Mountains, on Crow Reservation ground that's seen less oil and gas development than the flatter reservation land further east.
intro: The coalbed methane leasing that touched parts of the Crow Reservation in the 2000s concentrated more on the Powder River Basin's flatter, eastern extension than on the rougher ground near Pryor. That means most of the Pryor-area interests I run into are quiet — trust or fee land, depending on the specific family history, with little or no leasing activity on record. I confirm land status first either way, because that determines the entire process before value is even part of the conversation.
Chief Plenty Coups' home and the surrounding foothill country give this area its character, but that history doesn't change what's recorded, or not recorded, under the ground itself.

sections.heading: Terrain and why it matters here
paragraphs: Structural and access realities near the Pryor Mountains have made this corner of the reservation less attractive to CBM operators than the open ground further from the foothills. That's consistent with the thin leasing history I typically find on Pryor-area parcels.

sections.heading: Trust land, fee land, and what I check first
paragraphs: If your family's interest is trust land, any sale requires BIA approval and follows its own timeline. If it's fee land, I work through the Big Horn County Clerk and Recorder in Hardin. Either way, I confirm which situation applies before I say anything about what the interest might be worth.

sections.heading: Pricing quiet, untested ground fairly
paragraphs: Without a lease or drilling record to point to, I price a Pryor-area interest as long-term potential rather than pretending there's near-term activity that doesn't exist. I explain that reasoning plainly so you can decide with real information.

faqs.question: Is there oil or gas activity near Pryor?
faqs.answer: Limited, given the terrain and its distance from the more actively leased flatter reservation ground further east. I check your specific parcel regardless.

faqs.question: How do you determine if my interest is trust or fee land?
faqs.answer: I check both BIA and Big Horn County records using your family name and rough legal description.

faqs.question: Is a quiet, untested interest near Pryor worth selling?
faqs.answer: It can be, priced as long-term potential rather than current income. I explain that distinction clearly before making an offer.

faqs.question: Does the terrain near the Pryor Mountains mean drilling will never happen?
faqs.answer: Not never, but it's less likely than on the flatter reservation ground further east. I price interests against that realistic probability.

faqs.question: How do you price ground with no lease or production history at all?
faqs.answer: As long-term potential rather than current income. I lay out exactly how I arrive at that number before making an offer.
